sections.name: Tricky (Dino Domain's boss race)
sections.card:
Summary: The first world's boss, a triceratops you race in a car up a spiralling mountain in Dino Domain.
Looks like: A big red triceratops. Yellow stripes run along his back, and his yellow eyes have red irises.
Tips: Tricky has no tricks beyond charging forward, and if you bump into him he flattens you and you lose speed. Boulders tumble down the mountain from time to time, and the second race throws in extra boulders and falling pillars too. Weapon Balloons of two colours, red and blue, are placed on his course to help you out against him.
Tips: The race opens only once you have taken all the other courses in his world. Beat him and he sets you that world's Silver Coin challenges, and finishing them opens a harder rematch where he is faster, so use the balloons to win it. His Wizpig amulet piece comes only once you beat that second race.

sections.name: Bluey (Snowflake Mountain's boss race)
sections.card:
Summary: Snowflake Mountain's boss, a walrus you race in a hovercraft down an icy ski slope.
Looks like: A large blue walrus with a tuxedo piece at his neck, which the Nintendo DS remake leaves off.
Tips: The slope is jagged and lined with trees that get in your way. Just as Tricky does, he simply rushes forward, though he never squashes you.
Tips: The rematch only comes after you finish Snowflake Mountain's Silver Coin challenges. In it Bluey is faster, and a handful of snowballs also get in your way.

sections.name: Bubbler (Sherbet Island's boss race)
sections.card:
Summary: Sherbet Island's boss, an octopus you race in a hovercraft for three laps around a small island.
Weak points: You can shoot him. Red Weapon Balloons give you missiles to fire at him during the race.
Looks like: A large red octopus. His eyes are yellow, the irises green and the pupils black.
Tips: In the first race he scatters mines in the water around him, and hitting one trips you up.
Tips: In the rematch he is faster and trades the mines for huge bubbles that catch you and hold you for a while.

sections.name: Smokey (Dragon Forest's boss race)
sections.card:
Summary: Dragon Forest's boss, a dragon you race in a plane for three laps through caves and fields.
Looks like: An orange dragon whose belly, face and feet are yellow. His eyes are green, so he is the one boss that lacks yellow eyes.
Tips: He spits clouds of hot ash and drops puffs of fire behind him, and the fire can slow you down. In the rematch he flies faster and drops more of it.
Tips: Smokey Castle, the challenge level with his name, is not where you meet him, because he does not appear there.

sections.name: Taj's three vehicle races (Car, Hovercraft, Plane)
sections.card:
Summary: In Adventure Mode, Taj shows up after you have gathered enough Golden Balloons and calls you out to race him in a set vehicle. He rides a flying carpet, and beating him gives you one more Golden Balloon.
Weak points: He moves slowly in the Car Challenge, so that race is the easy one to win.
Looks like: A blue elephant who is also a genie and rides a magic red carpet.
Tips: The Hovercraft race is a little harder than the Car race, and the Plane race is rated the hardest of his three. The route is marked by red flags bearing the Nintendo 64 logo. Follow them, because straying a long way from the track disqualifies you.
Tips: Once a race is unlocked you can run it again whenever you like, but each one gives only a single Golden Balloon.

sections.name: T.T.'s ghosts (Time Trial)
sections.card:
Summary: In Tracks mode, Time Trial has you race T.T.'s best times. It is optional for the adventure, but beating him on every course is what makes T.T. playable.
Looks like: T.T. is an animated stopwatch. His shell is red on the outside with a yellow case inside, a blue button sits on top of his head, and his black arms and legs end in white gloves and shoes.
Tips: Each course has two times, an unlock time that brings out T.T.'s ghost and then a lower ghost time to beat. For example, Ancient Lake is 1:07.00 then 1:01.28, Fossil Canyon 1:37.00 then 1:30.16, Jungle Falls 1:08.00 then 1:02.50 and Hot Top Volcano 1:35.00 then 1:30.71.

sections.name: Silver Coins (the Silver Coin Challenge)
sections.card:
Summary: Eight coins to find on each course. Collect all eight and win the race to earn a Golden Balloon.
Uses: A world's challenges stay locked until you have won a race against its boss, and each course also needs its own minimum number of Golden Balloons before you can play its challenge. When you finish a challenge, Taj gives you a Golden Balloon.
Looks like: In the original game each coin has a colourful N64 icon on its sides.
Tips: Plenty of the coins are concealed well or lie outside the track.
Tips: Clearing the Silver Coin Challenge on all four courses of a world sets up the rematch with that world's boss. Adventure Two, a harder take on Adventure Mode, shifts the coins to other spots, and many are awkward to get to.

sections.name: Red Weapon Balloon (missiles)
sections.card:
Summary: The red Weapon Balloon gives missiles, and they get stronger the more red balloons you collect in a row, up to three levels.
Uses: One red balloon gives a missile that fires straight ahead, two give a homing missile and three give a volley of ten.
Looks like: Red, with yellow stars printed on it; the blue and green balloons carry yellow stars as well.
Tips: Being hit by a missile of any of the three levels makes you lose some bananas.

sections.name: Blue Weapon Balloon (speed boosts)
sections.card:
Summary: The blue Weapon Balloon gives a speed boost, in up to three levels.
Uses: One blue balloon gives a small boost, two give a larger one and three give the biggest. With a single balloon, letting go of the accelerator button while you use it gives a bigger boost.
Tips: In battle courses an item can only be upgraded once.
Tips: ROCKETFUEL is a cheat (a magic code, reached from the options menu) that turns every balloon blue.

sections.name: Yellow Weapon Balloon (shield)
sections.card:
Summary: The yellow Weapon Balloon gives a shield, in up to three levels.
Uses: The shield blocks hits, and any racer you bump into while it is up spins out. One balloon makes it short, two make it longer and three make it last the longest.
Looks like: A yellow balloon with purple stars printed on it.
Tips: BODYARMOR is a cheat (a magic code, reached from the options menu) that turns every balloon yellow.

sections.name: Green Weapon Balloon (oil, mines and bubbles)
sections.card:
Summary: The green Weapon Balloon gives something you drop, in up to three levels.
Uses: One green balloon gives an oil slick, or a gas cloud if you are in a plane. Two give a land mine, which floats for planes, and three give a bubble that snares whoever rides into it, floats them upward until it pops, and costs them a good deal of time.
Tips: Being hit by the second or third green item, the mine or the bubble, makes you lose some bananas.
Tips: TOXICOFFENDER is a cheat (a magic code, reached from the options menu) that turns every balloon green.

sections.name: Rainbow Weapon Balloon (magnet)
sections.card:
Summary: The rainbow Weapon Balloon gives a magnet, in up to three levels.
Uses: A single rainbow balloon gives a weak magnet that tugs you toward a racer ahead, if one is close enough. Two make the pull stronger and the range longer, and three give a powerful magnet that drags opponents back to you.
Tips: The weak magnet is yellow and the stronger one is red.
Tips: OPPOSITESATTRACT is a cheat (a magic code, reached from the options menu) that turns every balloon rainbow.

sections.name: Keys and the challenge levels
sections.card:
Summary: Four keys, one hidden on a course in each of the first four worlds, each opening the door to that world's challenge level.
Uses: The keys are in Ancient Lake in Dino Domain, Snowball Valley in Snowflake Mountain, Crescent Island in Sherbet Island and Boulder Canyon in Dragon Forest. A challenge level is an arena where you play against computer racers or other players, and winning one in Adventure Mode earns a piece of the T.T. amulet.
Tips: In Smokey Castle, a car level, you pick up bananas and deposit them in a treasure chest at the arena's centre, and the first to have ten in the chest wins. Fire Mountain is a plane level where you fly eggs from the middle lava pit to your nest and wait for them to hatch, while rivals can steal eggs or shoot missiles to spoil it. The first to hatch three eggs wins.
Tips: Icicle Pyramid (a car level) and Darkwater Beach (a hovercraft level) are won by being the last driver still in. You knock rivals out with weapons, and since bananas are your health, a driver with none left is out.

sections.name: Trophies from the Trophy Races
sections.card:
Summary: Each world's Trophy Race strings its four tracks together and scores points, and a high enough finish wins a trophy.
Uses: A bronze T.T. trophy is the prize for third place, a silver Taj trophy for second and a gold Wizpig trophy for first. You need four trophies in total to enter Future Fun Land.
Tips: A world's Trophy Race becomes available once you have beaten that world's boss for the second time. The computer racers in it are tougher than in a single race.
Tips: Trophy Races can also be played from Tracks mode, but only in the standard vehicle of each track.
